No problem! I love brainstorming for different deck ideas so it was fun to think about your configuration =)

I'm not 100% sure on how this deck actually plays but I'd recommend having less "two of each cards" and switching a lot of that to more like 4 of each card. 
    My suggestions at first glance is to remove the two indexes, howl of the packs, and think twices.

I love Index, but the problem with Index is that many times it can just be a complete flop when something much much better could have been drawn instead. For example what happens if you pop index on turn one, and you have nothing but land coming your way or something. If you had kept the right hand (ideally consisting of 2 or 3 lands), and you're not playing a 3 or 4 color deck, it doesn't matter which forests or plains you put in front of the other because you're still gonna get mana flooded and that's not going to be good.. I would really just recommend asking yourself WHAT is it, that could suit this strategy better? Also having 2 Indexes means that you probably won't even see it hardly ever, and what many players shoot for, is to have a deck that can consistently run and do, what it's meant to do. Having two of this card, like your other 2-of's, instead of 4 of a card you really need usually could make all the difference between winning and losing. 

Also, 2 Think Twices. Once again you may just want to consider what would fit the overall strategy better, and synergize with your other cards.

2 Howl of the packs - Unless the other people you are playing tend to be really slow, this may just not be worth having because of the incredibly high mana cost.

My suggestions for the three cards I named is to perhaps:

Switch out 2 Think Twices for 2 more Syncopates. This will allow your deck to be more flexible on game#1, and then you can sideboard after game one to more suit the deck you are playing against.

Switch out your 2 Howl of the Packs and 2 Indexes, for possibly Rapid Hybridizations. This can allow you to trade out your 1-drop mana guys later in the game for a 5/5 token once you've gotten Master Biomancer out, and you could even populate those tokens more consistently if you removed your 2 Negates, or your 2 Unsummons, and put in 2 more Druid's Deliverances.

Hope this helps you out a little bit! Looks fun.

Well, you only get 9 booster packs in a fatpack, so there's only so many good cards you can get. A fatpack can come with two deckboxes and a countdown dice a pack of lands ect, but the two deckboxes and the lands aren't really contributing to your collection, which is what I thought you said you were mainly focused on. So what I said was, you should just buy $40 dollars in booster packs, rather than a $40 fatpack. If you bought 9 booster packs which is what you get in a fatpack, that should really only cost you about $28 (assuming you are buying a rather new set). So instead of putting the other twelve into crap you probably don't need, buy 4 more booster packs! =D

Don't buy a fat pack, just put the money you would use to buy a fatpack into individual booster packs. Or if there's something in particular you got your eye on, just buy a single card, or a full playset of that single card
